chunks: My father and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah have mercy on them both) said: Sa'd ibn Abd Allah narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated to us, from Ali ibn Abd Allah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Barqi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding the Word of Allah, the Mighty and High: 'And they will swear by Allah, 'If we had been able, we would certainly have gone forth with you,' they cause their own souls to perish, and Allah knows that they are liars.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Allah, the Mighty and High, refuted their statement: 'If we had been able, we would certainly have gone forth with you,' stating that they indeed had the capability to go forth.'

key_terms.أَكْذَبَهُمُ اللَّهُ: Allah refuted them / Made their statement false
key_terms.يُهْلِكُوا أَنفُسَهُمْ: They cause their own souls to perish

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about the claim 'If we had been able' in Surah Al-Imran?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Tawhid*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) elucidates the concept of *Qudra* (capability) by refuting the hypocrites' excuse in Surah Al-Imran that they lacked the ability to join the Prophet. The Imam asserts that their claim of inability was false, as they were physically and materially capable, thereby highlighting that their failure stemmed from a lack of faith rather than external constraints. This interpretation underscores the Shia theological principle that divine capability is often present, but human will and conviction determine its actualization.

en.sayed-ali-raza-rizvi: 16. My father and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (RA) both said: Sa`d ibn `Abd Allah said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn `Isa said, on the authority of `Ali ibn `Abd Allah, on the authority of Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Barqi that Abu `Abd Allah al-Sadiq (AS) was asked to interpret the Word of Allah, the Mighty and High: And they swear by Allah: If we had been able, we would certainly have gone forth with you; they cause their own souls t perish, and Allah knows that they are most surely liars.
He (AS) said: “Allah, the Mighty and High, has refuted their statement: If we had been able, we would certainly have gone forth with you; stating that they did indeed have the means of going forth.”
